method: Both arms evaluated with the same simulate_next_day() function. Baseline uses recorded CSV settings. Tejas arm calls optimise() on each day's state and re-evaluates the recommended settings with the same simulator.
limitation: The optimizer's objective function IS the simulator, so Tejas cannot appear worse on simulated metrics. Any improvement is within-model and optimistic — not a real field result. All data is synthetic.
energy_note: SPM now affects production (min of reservoir inflow and pump capacity). The optimizer chooses SPM=4.0-9.95 (mean 5.32). On 118/180 days it still picks SPM=4.0 — these are cold high-viscosity days where reservoir inflow is already low and the pump is never the bottleneck at any SPM. On hotter days it raises SPM to avoid oil loss from pump-limitation. The energy reduction is real within the model but optimistic as a field prediction.

assumptions.cycle_prod_progress: days_since_steam_injection / max(days_since_steam_injection per cycle), clamped 0-1, zero on non-production days
assumptions.vfd: Both arms use the recorded vfd_frequency_hz (optimizer holds VFD fixed at 42 Hz during grid search but the evaluation call uses the row's actual VFD)
assumptions.injection_pressure: Passed to simulator only on injection days; NaN rows treated as None
